sentence: This project studies how repeated cocaine use weakens an inhibitory signaling pathway in the prefrontal cortex of mice and whether strengthening it reverses addiction-like changes.
This project builds enzyme-based methods for making antibodies with altered sugar attachments, and antibody-drug conjugates, to treat human diseases.
This project studies how a transporter protein in the malaria parasite works and changes, to understand and predict resistance to malaria drugs.
This project builds hydrogel materials in which specific cell types can change their nearby surroundings to help blood vessels or bone form.
This project studies how neurons lose synaptic connections and which cellular and circuit changes cause movement problems in spinal muscular atrophy.
This project tests drugs in a mouse model and in stem cell derived cells to find out how pulmonary arteriovenous malformations form and shrink.
This project provides human intestinal enteroid and colonoid cultures, and builds co-culture models with immune cells, to study how bacterial infections affect the gut.
This project builds a tool that predicts cancer risk in patients with inflammatory muscle disease and uses liquid biopsy to study cancer and outcomes.
This project studies how DNA-damaging transposons contribute to cancer, including the change from Barrett's esophagus to esophageal cancer, by mapping the DNA rearrangements they cause.
This project builds deep learning tools that use abdominal computed tomography scans and medical records to predict a patient's risk of future cardiovascular disease.
This project studies how lung healing works, looking at mitochondrial calcium and histone methylation, to help find treatments for chronic respiratory diseases.
This project sequences the whole genomes of Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica bacteria collected from companion and food animals.
This project studies how proteins linked to polyglutamine diseases are controlled in whole animals and human cells to find ways to protect neurons.
This project tries to find genes that control how opioid drugs act in C. elegans, to help reduce harmful side effects of opioids.
This project studies how the protein EZH2 acts in tumor cells and T-cells to make T-cell therapies work better against cancer.
This project combines DNA proximity ligation assays and genome alignments to find which DNA elements evolve together and how they interact.
This project studies whether blood flow restriction therapy improves muscle quality and shoulder function after a rotator cuff injury.
This project studies how androgens help the immune system attack endocrine tumors and tests hormone therapy combined with immune checkpoint blockade.
This project builds self-assembling peptide nanomaterials that prompt antibodies against a key driver of chronic rhinosinusitis, and tests them in mouse models.
This project studies whether a receptor protein helps bunyaviruses enter host cells, to find targets for treating these viruses.
